title: Lord, How Delightful 'Tis to See
description: Lord, How Delightful 'Tis to See in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 95 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Joy and Blessing of Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, how de-light-ful 'tis to see A whole as-sem-bly wor-ship thee; At once they sing, at once they pray, They hear of heaven and learn the way.

lines: At once they sing, at once they pray,
They hear of heaven and learn the way.
O, write upon our memory, Lord,
The text and doctrines of thy word:
That we may break thy laws no more,
But love thee better than before.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
